title: Afghanistan to Host India in Historic T20I Series in Delhi Ahead of Asian Games
excerpt: The three-match series at the Arun Jaitley Stadium marks the first time Afghanistan hosts India on Indian soil, with both teams using it as preparation for the 2026 Asian Games.
body:
• Afghanistan will host India for three T20Is at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi in mid-September 2026, marking the first time Afghanistan hosts India on Indian soil.
  • The series serves as preparation for both teams ahead of the 2026 Asian Games cricket competition, which begins September 23 in Nagoya, Japan.
  • India's white-ball tour of Bangladesh has been rescheduled to September 2026, with three ODIs and three T20Is confirmed between September 1 and 13.

Afghanistan will officially host India for the first time on Indian soil when the two nations meet for a three-match T20I series at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi in September. The matches, scheduled for mid-September, carry symbolic weight: the Afghan Cricket Board has long played its home fixtures in India and the UAE due to security concerns at home, but this marks the first bilateral where Afghanistan is the designated host against India.

A Historic Bilateral on Borrowed Ground

The Afghanistan Cricket Board has used venues in Dehradun, Greater Noida, and Lucknow as home grounds for years, along with stadiums in the United Arab Emirates. The BCCI and the Delhi and District Cricket Association coordinated to make the Arun Jaitley Stadium available for the series.

The arrangement extends a decades-old pattern forced by Afghanistan's domestic security challenges. While the ACB has hosted other nations on Indian soil before, facing India itself in this setup is unprecedented.

"While the ACB has hosted other nations on Indian soil before, facing India itself in this setup is unprecedented."

Asian Games Preparation

The timing is deliberate. The 2026 Asian Games cricket competition begins September 23 in Nagoya, Japan, and both teams will use this series as a warm-up. India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka have already secured direct entry into the men's cricket knockout stage after the draw was announced on July 24, according to Reuters. Afghanistan will compete in the preliminary round alongside Nepal, Japan, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and Oman.

All matches in Nagoya will be played in the T20 format, making this bilateral series a natural preparation window. India swept both gold medals at the 2022 Asian Games held in Hangzhou in 2023.

India's Dominance in the Head-to-Head Record

India and Afghanistan have faced each other in nine T20I matches, with India winning eight. The lone exception was a no-result match. The most dramatic encounter came in Bengaluru in January 2024, when both sides finished level on 212 in regulation before India won the Super Over.

Virat Kohli leads the run-scorers in this matchup with 225 runs in six matches at a strike rate of 159.57, including an unbeaten 122 against Afghanistan at the 2022 Asia Cup — the highest individual score in this head-to-head.

India's Packed September Schedule

The Afghanistan series is part of a congested calendar for India. The BCCI confirmed earlier this year that India's white-ball tour of Bangladesh, originally scheduled for August 2025, has been deferred to September 2026. The Indian team will arrive in Bangladesh on August 28, with three ODIs on September 1, 3, and 6, followed by three T20Is on September 9, 12, and 13.

After Bangladesh, the team pivots to the Afghanistan T20Is and then the Asian Games — three assignments in roughly four weeks. India's national selection committee will need to manage workloads carefully, particularly with the IPL ending in late May and a packed England tour in July preceding this stretch.

What's Next

Exact dates for the Delhi T20Is are expected to be confirmed by the ACB and BCCI in the coming weeks. For Afghanistan, the series offers a morale boost as the team continues its rise in global T20 cricket. For India, it is the final tune-up before a continental title defense in Nagoya.
